questions.question: What does the 'three-face set method' use to deduce information about a die?
options: Only a single visible face
The three faces visible in a single view, since they must all be mutually adjacent
The die's physical weight
The color of the die
questions.rationale: Since the three faces visible in one view of a die must all be mutually adjacent (meeting at a shared corner), this set provides strong constraints for further deductions.

questions.question: What is 'fast opposite-face detection' based on?
options: Randomly guessing which faces are opposite
Always assuming the highest and lowest numbers are opposite
If a face never appears in any of the given views alongside a specific other face, and all other faces have been accounted for, the two are likely opposite
Measuring the physical distance between faces
questions.rationale: By process of elimination across multiple views, if two faces are never seen together and every other pairing has been accounted for, they can be quickly identified as opposite.

questions.question: On a 'standard' die (as conventionally used in most exam questions, unless stated otherwise), what do opposite faces typically sum to?
questions.rationale: By long-standing convention, a standard die's opposite faces sum to 7: 1-6, 2-5, and 3-4.

questions.question: What does 'clockwise order' of three faces around a corner describe?
options: The order in which the faces were painted
The order the faces are listed in the question
The alphabetical order of the face labels
The sequence in which the three visible faces appear when read in a clockwise direction around that shared corner
questions.rationale: Clockwise order describes the specific rotational sequence of the three faces as viewed around their shared corner, which distinguishes different valid arrangements.

questions.question: Why does the clockwise vs anticlockwise order of faces around a corner matter?
options: It distinguishes between two dice that show the same three faces but are actually mirror images (different arrangements) of each other
It never actually matters
It only matters for symbol dice, not numbered ones
It determines the die's physical size
questions.rationale: Two dice can show the identical three faces at a corner but in opposite rotational order — that difference means they are mirror-image (distinct) arrangements, not the same die.

questions.question: What is the difference between a 'rotation' and a 'reflection' of a die?
options: They are the same thing
A reflection is just a rotation by 90 degrees
A rotation preserves the die's actual arrangement (it's still the same physical die, just turned), while a reflection produces a mirror-image arrangement that is a genuinely different die layout
Rotations only apply to symbol dice
questions.rationale: A rotation simply reorients the same physical die; a reflection produces a mirror-image layout that represents a fundamentally different (non-identical) die arrangement.

questions.question: Why is distinguishing rotation from reflection important in dice reasoning?
options: It never actually matters for solving problems
Because two views that look similar might represent either the same die rotated, or two different (mirror-image) dice, and treating them the same would lead to an incorrect answer
Because reflections are always invalid
Because only rotations are tested in exams
questions.rationale: Confusing a mirror-image (reflected) arrangement for a simple rotation of the same die can lead to incorrectly concluding two views represent the same die when they don't.

questions.question: What is a 'vector/coordinate model' of a cube used for?
options: Measuring the cube's weight
Replacing the need to know opposite face pairs
Only used for symbol dice
Assigning coordinate axes to the cube's faces or directions, allowing rotations and face relationships to be reasoned about mathematically rather than just visually
questions.rationale: A coordinate model assigns axes to the cube's faces/directions, enabling rotations and relationships to be reasoned about with mathematical precision rather than relying solely on visualization.

questions.question: In a coordinate model, how might the three pairs of opposite faces of a cube be naturally represented?
options: As the positive and negative directions along three perpendicular axes (x, y, z)
As three unrelated random points
As a single combined axis
As angles measured in degrees only
questions.rationale: The three opposite-face pairs map naturally onto the positive and negative directions of three perpendicular coordinate axes (x, y, z).

questions.question: Why is a vector/coordinate model useful for advanced dice reasoning problems?
options: It has no practical use
It allows rotations and orientations to be tracked and computed precisely, rather than relying only on visual intuition
It only works for very simple, single-view problems
It replaces the need for the opposite-face rule
questions.rationale: For complex, multi-rotation problems, a coordinate model allows precise, computable tracking of orientation, reducing the reliance on error-prone visual intuition alone.
